headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: shared filesystem plus broad write/network privileges make Goose↔Replit Agent unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and Goose explicitly shares state via filesystem while Replit Agent persists workspace files across sessions. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's files as trusted input. No direct shared clipboard/MCP channel is documented, so I do not escalate higher.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other's generated files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace is used for handoff, attacker-controlled file content can steer the other agent.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Require a human review step before one agent consumes the other's output files.
Prefix handoff files with a strict schema and reject free-form text.
Disable automatic file-watching or auto-import behaviors.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content filtering at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Both have broad filesystem access and broad network egress, so sensitive data can flow from one agent's workspace into the other's outputs or remote calls. The pair's shared filesystem-style state makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are present in the Replit workspace, Goose can read them if pointed at the same files.
IF Goose or Replit Agent forwards workspace contents to configured model providers or APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Use separate workspaces for code and secrets.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after cross-agent use.
Restrict network egress during handoff tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, read and write the filesystem, and use broad network egress. Goose shares state via filesystem and Replit Agent's workspace persists across sessions, so concurrent writes to the same repo or Repl can race and corrupt git or files. This matches the rubric's high-risk overlap pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or rewrites can conflict.
IF both agents install packages in the same environment, dependency state can diverge or break.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize write operations with a simple lock file.
Have only one agent modify git state at a time.
Snapshot the workspace before parallel edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce shell, file, and MCP-driven outputs that Replit Agent may treat as task context, and both are coding agents that can act on generated artifacts. However, Replit Agent is not documented here as blindly trusting Goose, so I keep this at medium rather than high. The pathway exists in default workflows when one agent hands files to the other without verification.
conditions: IF Goose-generated files are fed into Replit Agent as task context, errors can cascade.
IF Replit Agent executes code or deployment changes based on Goose's unverified outputs, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before acting on another agent's output.
Use checklists for code, config, and deployment changes.
Compare outputs against source-of-truth files before execution.
Limit one agent to drafting and the other to execution.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens on-machine. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches between local machine storage and Replit-managed cloud storage. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in both the local Goose environment and the Replit workspace, retention controls may diverge.
IF EU personal data or PHI is moved into Replit without a matching policy, residency or compliance obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair's shared workflow.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
Delete temporary files after each task.
Use separate storage locations for secrets and code.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across environments.
